name: Alibaba PolarDB
tagline: Alibaba Cloud's shared-storage relational service in MySQL-, PostgreSQL- and Oracle-compatible editions.
description: PolarDB is Alibaba Cloud's cloud-native relational database, conceptually similar to Amazon Aurora: compute nodes share a distributed storage layer (PolarFS) over RDMA, so read nodes can be added in minutes without copying data. It comes in PolarDB for MySQL, PolarDB for PostgreSQL and an Oracle-compatible PostgreSQL edition, with serverless scaling, an in-memory column index (IMCI) for analytics and Global Database Network for cross-region reads. A separate distributed edition, PolarDB-X, handles shared-nothing sharding. It is the default high-end relational choice inside Alibaba Cloud, especially in China and Southeast Asia; outside that ecosystem it offers little reason to switch.

pricing.notes: Pay-as-you-go or subscription per node plus storage; serverless billed per PCU; periodic Alibaba Cloud free trials.

scale.notes: One primary with up to 15 read nodes on shared storage (hundreds of TB); multi-master and PolarDB-X options for write scale-out; GDN for cross-region reads.

strengths: Shared storage over RDMA lets read nodes be added in minutes without data copies
In-memory column index (IMCI) speeds analytics on transactional tables
MySQL, PostgreSQL and Oracle-compatible editions under one service
Serverless scaling and Global Database Network for cross-region reads
Flashback query to recover from accidental writes
weaknesses: Single writer per cluster unless you move to multi-master or PolarDB-X
English documentation and community resources are thinner than AWS/GCP equivalents
Feature parity differs between MySQL and PostgreSQL editions
useCases: E-commerce and gaming backends on Alibaba Cloud
Read-heavy apps needing fast replica scaling
